paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 3, halakhah 7, and Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot, chapter 7, halakhah 7; Hyman suggests that the reading should be “Rabbi Elazar in the name of R' Chanina.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: The abbreviation ר״א in the proposed reading is rendered Elazar after the heading.

The two whole Guggenheimer paragraphs, Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:7 and Ketubot 7:7, fully name Rabbi Laazar or Elazar bar Haninah. They support Elazar’s own full title; the father’s unexpanded title remains R' in the new proposed reading. They do not adopt Hyman’s tentative in-the-name-of emendation. Hyman’s Chanina form and both locators remain, the existing abbreviation note stays verbatim, and no father-versus-transmission relationship is merged.
